title: Build, buy, or adopt open source: the comparison that runs three years out

videos.script: Coreto's search box is bad, and buyers notice. Type the name of a band with one letter wrong and you find nothing. {{search}} The Catalogue team has three ways out. Build better search on the database Coreto already runs. Buy a hosted search service. Or adopt an open-source search engine and run it on their own servers. {{options}} Most teams settle this in a meeting, on the price of the first year. That number misleads, because the three options spend their money at different times. One pays most of it up front. One pays a bill that rises every year. One pays in engineers' hours, every month, for as long as it runs. {{years}} So this lesson puts all three in your spreadsheet, side by side, three years out. Buying wins, by less than you would guess, and its lead shrinks every year. {{sheet}} Before the arithmetic comes a question that settles many of these decisions on its own. Is search the reason venues choose Coreto, or something it simply has to do well? {{core}}
